name: Supremacism
summary: Supremacism holds that one group is superior to all others and should have authority over them, on grounds such as race, religion or nation. In its best-documented modern form, white supremacism, it ranks races by innate capacity, opposes equality and race mixing, seeks restricted immigration and segregated or racially defined states, and has justified slavery, colonialism and genocide.
scope: Profile of white supremacism as the dominant strand, drawing on Stoddard and Grant (1920), Stephens' Cornerstone Speech, Jim Crow and Nazi racial law, and modern white nationalism. It excludes other supremacisms (religious, male, Han, Hutu, Black) which would differ on religion, gender and nation, and economic questions are largely unaddressed and answered with low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: No documented programme; adherents typically resent state benefits that reach the groups they target, so a lean against is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Economic policy is secondary to race; the movement's right-wing mainstream leans against wage mandates, inferred from its general economics.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: White nationalists are split between market-friendly and anti-capitalist, anti-banker strands, and race is the organizing principle.

public-ownership.rationale: Not a theme in supremacist writing; inferred lean against from the American strands rooted in property-holding and states' rights.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Populist anti-elite rhetoric and defence of property pull in opposite directions, and sources do not give a common line.

unions-good.rationale: Historically racial exclusion from unions and hostility to organised labor in the US strands; inferred, not documented in the sources.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Confederate order rested on property including enslaved people; other strands say little, so a mild lean is inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Strands split between anti-corporate populism and deregulation; race, not corporate policy, defines the movement.

cut-welfare.rationale: Adherents claim immigration brings dependency and want welfare reserved for the in-group; the lean is inferred from that.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialist-style economics is rejected as Marxist or internationalist; inferred from opposition to class framing.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents distrust the federal state yet back security powers against targeted groups; no common position documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the order-and-purity outlook of the traditionalist strands; not documented.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents condemn such laws as suppression of their views and of white identity.

strong-leader.rationale: Nazism's leader principle and the Confederate hierarchy favour strong command, but US strands are anti-government; a mild lean.

state-harmful.rationale: The aim is a white state or ethnostate, so the state is wanted as a racial instrument even where the current one is hated.

limit-guns.rationale: Armed-citizenry culture in US strands; inferred, and Nazi Germany disarmed targeted groups only.

empower-police-military.rationale: Order-oriented strands back coercive authority, though anti-federal militias dissent; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, family-centred outlook; not directly documented.

rehabilitation.rationale: Punitive views on crime and lynching tradition suggest a lean against; not documented as doctrine.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents tie white survival to family formation and high white birth rates, which makes the family central.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The movement lists LGBTQ+ people among its targets and champions traditional family norms.

abortion-legal.rationale: Concern over falling white birth rates favours restriction, though eugenic strands accept selective abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents include Christian Identity, pagans and atheists, so religion's public role genuinely divides them.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial hierarchy is held to be natural, so remedial programmes are rejected as unjust or mistaken.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A biologically fixed order is the general premise; inferred rather than quoted for gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: White nationalists hold that culture stems from race and seek preservation of white culture and majorities.

gradual-change.rationale: Radical strands want overthrow and a white homeland; established institutions are not revered.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Grant warns immigrants will drive out native Americans, and white nationalists want immigration limited to Europeans.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Grant ridicules internationalism as a vain phantom and the movement champions racial nations over world bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Nationalist and anti-globalist stance suggests opposition; not documented in detail.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalist orientation with priority to the in-group, though white solidarity can cross borders.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Hostility to universalism and to non-white causes; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Directly opposed to the entire immigration-restriction and racial-preservation programme.

limit-growth.rationale: Ecofascist and pro-growth strands both exist; no shared position.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from anti-globalist, anti-elite positioning; not documented.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No doctrine; strands range from technophile to back-to-nature.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from pro-industrial, pro-security nationalism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Secession in 1861, militant post-1960s groups seeking to overthrow the federal government and a white homeland.

experts-over-public.rationale: Distrust of academic and media elites; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Rejection of socialism is general; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred rejection of socialist designs; not documented.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from property orientation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Family continuity and lineage are valued; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Opposed to state transfers that adherents see as benefiting non-whites; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism common to white nationalists; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nazi-style dirigisme versus American free-market strands; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Marxist abolitionism is incompatible with hierarchy and property; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Banker conspiracy themes are common, so a mild lean is inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Nazi corporatism versus modern movements that do not address it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nazism yes, but modern and US strands do not demand it; split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not a central issue; inferred lean against from republican American strands.

democracy-best.rationale: Grant argues democracy works only among a homogeneous Nordic people, so it is not best when voters differ racially.

workers-councils.rationale: Opposed to class-based, internationalist socialism; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Confederacy's secession and white-homeland projects imply a right to separate.

natural-rulers.rationale: The core belief is that one group is superior and should have authority over others.

political-violence-never.rationale: The movement has a history of lynching, terror and attacks such as Christchurch, and does not renounce violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nazis exalted war, but Stoddard and Grant lament wars among whites as suicidal.

separate-church-state.rationale: Christian Identity versus secular and pagan adherents.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian Identity yes; other adherents are pagan or atheist.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred; the movement wants the state as the racial guardian.

military-superiority.rationale: Stoddard frames world politics as racial rivalry, which suggests wanting strength, but this is inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: White nationalists want majority-white states or a white ethnostate.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Stoddard calls race the basic factor in world affairs, displacing class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Supremacism is opposed to equality in any form.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The record of colonial and settler domination implies rejection; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Colonialism is defended or justified by the ideology, so owing reparations is rejected.

civilizational-union.rationale: Stoddard urges white solidarity beyond national borders after the white civil war.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Group interest is moral, individual self-interest less clear; split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Group-first thinking; inferred from rejection of individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No position except in ecofascist strands.

limit-population.rationale: Adherents want to raise white birth rates; may support limits abroad, so only a mild lean.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Civilizational achievement is attributed to the dominant race; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Grant and Stoddard seek to restore white dominance they see slipping, and neo-Confederates defend the old order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: An ideology of fixed hierarchy; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Militants favour it, electoral nationalists do not.

means-match-ends.rationale: Violent and coercive tactics are used without regard to ends; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Civilizational superiority claims conflict with it; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist doctrine, rejected by adherents who stress race over class.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class rule of workers contradicts racial hierarchy.

collective-farming.rationale: Opposed to collectivisation as a Bolshevik policy; Grant links Bolshevism to foreign leadership.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Stoddard sees racial rivalry, not capitalism, as the source of conflict.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anti-federal strands agree, state-oriented strands do not.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred; adherents back state restriction for racial and moral order.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are tied to group membership and rank, not held equally by individuals.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed by supremacist sources; no basis for a lean.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred; citizenship is racial belonging, not a customer relation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Conspiratorial claims about media and academia are common among adherents.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Grant and Stoddard rank races by innate capacity; scientific racism is a root of the ideology.

total-state.rationale: Nazism yes; American strands distrust big government.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nazi rebirth rhetoric and later calls for a white renaissance; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nazi Lebensraum versus modern separatists seeking a homeland; split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not part of the ideology; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Slavery was defended, but the statement concerns serfdom tied to land; weak inference.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Adherents claim objective racial science; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Grant says ideals cannot be entrusted to other races, implying ideals bound to race.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Many white nationalists oppose Israel or Zionism, though some draw parallels with it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Ancestry-based membership logic suggests support; not documented.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from support for segregated or private schooling in some traditions.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred; the movement relies on law and force.

national-self-determination.rationale: Applies to the in-group: white peoples governing themselves in their own states.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Pagan, atheist and Christian adherents differ.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: White nationalists want public benefits limited to the in-group and oppose immigrant access.

class-collaboration.rationale: Racial unity over class conflict; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Heritage is the racial and civilizational inheritance to be defended.

dominated-front.rationale: Stoddard treats Asian and colonial solidarity as a menace to white power.

workers-nation.rationale: National rather than international class organisation; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditionalist gender order and male-supremacist overlap; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Nazi anti-interest rhetoric but no general doctrine.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Jim Crow, apartheid and the Nuremberg Laws are canonical expressions, and modern separatists seek separation.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative alignment.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Culture is held to follow race, so non-whites are not seen as assimilable.

elite-replacement.rationale: White nationalists claim immigration and multiculturalism threaten whites, calling it white genocide.

national-mission.rationale: Colonial White Man's Burden versus modern separatists; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Nazism drew on eugenics and Grant ties national strength to population quality.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from sympathy with state coercion.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Grant calls interracial unions suicide, and anti-miscegenation laws were justified by white supremacy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Stephens declared the foundation to be that the Black man is not equal to the white man.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not a question the ideology engages with.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler and colonial rule was justified, so adherents reject the label; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Stephens rejected the Founders' equality premise, and authority follows race, not general consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Some white nationalists support remigration of non-white minorities.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Stoddard frames world history as racial struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Opposed to state action against nationalist parties; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Domination of other groups is the goal.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Grant argues institutions work only in a homogeneous population and warns against mixing races.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian strands yes, anti-government strands no.

party-controls-media.rationale: Adherents want their own views heard; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred; Nazism aside, not a demand.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: They want citizenship narrower than a mere wait; inferred lean for.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Hostile to internationalism, though pan-white unity appeals to some.

clerical-rule.rationale: Not a general position; adherents are not mainly clerical rule advocates.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Grant and Stoddard want white nations to unite, not undermine their war efforts.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Nazi suppression of art versus free-speech rhetoric today.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Nationalist isolationism in many strands; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed militia culture in US strands; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Blood-and-soil themes in Nazism; weaker elsewhere.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Races and civilizations are ranked, with Nordics at the top.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Christian Identity yes, pagan and atheist adherents no.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The 1790 Naturalization Act limited citizenship to whites and white nationalists seek ethnic membership.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Minority protections are not a goal; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from conformity to racial and traditional order.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from rejection of aid to poor nations.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Stoddard sees non-white populations as a threat, not as recipients of white duty.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The question is internal to the left.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Confederate secession tradition implies the opposite.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Not part of Western supremacism; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Race is held to determine capacity, so innate nature dominates.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred; Confederate law and Jim Crow were legalist.

leader-cult.rationale: Nazi cult versus modern strands; split.

refugee-return.rationale: Opposed to inward migration and to return rights of non-nationals; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Nazi expansion on that basis; modern separatists less so.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not a position of Western supremacism; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Stoddard and Grant call for kindred white or Nordic peoples to unite.

decide-locally.rationale: States' rights underlay the Confederacy, but nation-wide white-state projects centralise; strands split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: White nationalist strands want a racially defined state rather than minority self-government inside a shared one; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Supremacists reject equal rights for the groups they rank lower, and white nationalism seeks remigration or separate states instead.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Stoddard and Grant treat race and heredity as the driver of civilisations, not economic conditions.

ban-cartels.rationale: Economic policy is secondary to race and varies widely across strands, so no settled position is documented.

no-bailouts.rationale: No documented position; adherents are split between market and nationalist economics.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from the Jim Crow era, which used majoritarian white rule to override minority claims, and from hostility to courts protecting minorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the traditional gender hierarchy common in supremacist movements; not a defining position.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from the economic nationalism of fascist and white nationalist strands; not defining.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Stoddard and later strands oppose internationalism, so binding international standards are inferred to be rejected.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's hierarchical, interest-based economics.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Documented violence and some accelerationist strands favour direct action, but many adherents prefer politics, so this is contested.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine itself ranks groups by birth, so it opposes abolishing inherited status, though titles are not addressed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: White supremacist writers centre history on the white race and its civilisation, as in Stoddard.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Supremacism and colonial ideology hold the superior group may rule others, and Stoddard defends white world-dominance.

patriotic-education.rationale: Adherents favour pride in their own group and nation; inferred from white nationalism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Supremacism rejects racial equality (Stephens, Stoddard), so ending racial preferences for minorities fits.

public-money-creation.rationale: Economic questions are largely unaddressed; adherents are inferred as split.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Economic questions are largely unaddressed; adherents are inferred as split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Stoddard and colonial supremacists favour keeping control over former dominions; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: No documented line; inferred as neutral.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Adherents hold that all workers of the favoured group share a stake in dominance, but typically deny exploitation framing; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Adherents typically defend freedom to exclude, as in segregationist and white nationalist arguments; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Supremacists reject equal-rights limits on the dominant group, and Jim Crow worked around constitutional limits; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: white supremacists defended the colonial order and the borders it drew.

elective-rulers.rationale: Adherents are split between elective forms, as in the Confederacy, and hereditary or racial-elite rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: Southern segregationists defended state and minority vetoes, though this is not a central doctrine.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Supremacists justified secession and resistance, but also demanded obedience to racial hierarchy; no common line.

parliament-supreme.rationale: No settled position; some strands favour assemblies and others strongman or monarchic rule.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the doctrine concerns human hierarchy, and animal welfare is not part of it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: animal use is accepted as part of the natural order the doctrine assumes.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalist duty toward inferiors appears in Southern thought, but modern strands do not stress it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the movement demands political action to secure group dominance.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: adherents see mass media as controlled by hostile groups, though not as pacifying the people.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: No documented position on consent versus force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the doctrine explains national wealth by racial capacity rather than exploitation.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: white nationalism limits full citizenship, and so office, to the favoured group.

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns communist parties, which supremacism does not address.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the movement favours national and racial self-sufficiency over dependence.

return-lost-territory.rationale: No common line; claims depend on the nation or race involved.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The doctrine holds that the superior group rules, so rule by non-settler peoples over settlers is rejected.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: White supremacism is the movement antifascism opposes, and adherents reject it as a founding value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Many adherents admire fascism while opposing communism, so equivalence is not accepted uniformly.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The Lost Cause line denies slavery as cause, though the Cornerstone Speech says the opposite; adherents lean toward the denial.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: defending Confederate and similar monuments is a common stance.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: adherents oppose feminist framing and welcome claims of male disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: adherents oppose feminist framing and welcome claims of male victimhood.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Stoddard and Grant hold that races differ in capacity, so one institutional model does not fit all.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Supremacist strands vary between authoritarian regimes and civilian segregationist rule.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred at low confidence: the movement favours traditional gender roles over paying for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the traditional family order white nationalist movements defend; not addressed directly in the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Hierarchy by innate ability fits merit, but the sources stress race and rank over competitive examination; no clear position.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist and protectionist outlook of white nationalism.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalism and pronatalism of white nationalism.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Stoddard distrusts democracy and mass government, so binding recall by voters is unlikely, though racial in-group democracy was practised.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Economic policy is secondary; inferred a mild lean against private markets in pensions among nationalist state-welfare supporters.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: movements defend private property and have no communal-land doctrine, only racial control of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: White supremacist regimes such as Jim Crow states and the Confederacy kept legislatures for the dominant group.

single-official-language.rationale: White nationalism seeks an ethnostate with a single dominant culture and language, so a mild yes is inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: White supremacist systems restricted land ownership by race, and white nationalism seeks racially defined territory.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The doctrine rejects racial equality, so treating unequal racial outcomes as discrimination contradicts its premise.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents vary between traditionalist anti-materialism and capitalism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: adherents are split between nationalist non-intervention and support for kindred white causes abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the colonial and great-power domination the doctrine justified.

corporate-influence.rationale: Economic questions are largely unaddressed; supremacists attack elites and finance but do not clearly take a side on lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from white nationalism's hostility to outside influence on the nation and to globalist networks.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: White nationalism treats falling white birth rates as a threat, so it backs measures that raise them over immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not a defining issue; local residency limits are not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: welfare and state employment sit uneasily with its opposition to welfare and equality, though it favours jobs for the dominant group.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: it rejects spreading democracy and equal standing of peoples, so democracy promotion is no route to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: it prizes order and hierarchy and backs the law that upholds the dominant group, though it rejects laws that mandate equality.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: Stoddard-style thinking supports dominant powers ruling other peoples, so a ban on intervention is unlikely.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: unions are opposed or kept racially exclusive, so industrial organisation across groups is not wanted.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: White supremacism is defined in part by the belief in a hidden minority, usually Jews, plotting against the white nation, as in replacement conspiracies.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: it upholds the traditional family and sees marriage as the basis of racial continuity, so it would not abolish legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrust government but favour secrecy for their own movement.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from its attachment to rural, blood-and-soil life and economic self-reliance.

informal-organisation.rationale: Adherents are split between formal parties and leaderless, small-cell organising.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to international bodies and its emphasis on national sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: White nationalism defines the nation by race and ancestry, not religion, though Christian identity strands exist.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: Stoddard's white world-supremacy envisages a dominant group whose primacy others acknowledge.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: No documented position on regional revenue; strands differ between centralist and states'-rights positions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: supremacists defend private property and oppose communism, so personal belongings are secure.

defeat-communism.rationale: White supremacist movements from the Nazis to modern groups have been strongly anti-communist.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; no shared view on public service delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: Strands differ, with many Christian or pagan, and few endorse a materialist view of religion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: No documented position; strands range from capitalist to anti-capitalist.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Supremacist strands generally reject gender equality and favour traditional roles; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: traditional family roles and distrust of state benefits make socialised care unwelcome.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed in the main texts; strands differ.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: white supremacist rule historically overrode treaties with indigenous peoples, e.g. in the US.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: communal property conflicts with the individualist, hierarchical emphasis of the main strands.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: ethnostate and Lebensraum ideas favour settlement by the dominant group.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Some strands, notably fascism, claim a third way while others align with capitalism; split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: White nationalists claim homelands for their race through ancestry, but the core idea is racial rank, so this is inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial is widespread among modern white supremacists and neo-Nazis, but the early theorists in scope predate it and adherents differ.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not central; white supremacist groups are typically hostile to homosexuality, though some are not, and the Nazi state criminalised it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Jim Crow and Nazi rule suppressed political opposition and the movement seeks order under the dominant group, as the Wikipedia article describes.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Adherents split between Christian identity strands and pagan or secular racialists, so there is no common stance.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Supremacist doctrine justified colonial rule over lower races for the benefit of the ruling nation, as Stoddard and Grant and the white supremacy article show.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not part of white supremacism; the strand in scope sees Islam and Muslims as an out-group, so a duty of Muslim resistance is rejected, inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not a supremacist position; religious-law legitimacy conflicts with race-based rule, inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The ideology defines rule by the dominant group; broad popular participation by all is not its aim, inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Supremacism denies equal worth among groups and rejects that racism is an oppression to be fought; it opposes this framing.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not central, but white supremacist movements are overwhelmingly hostile to transgender recognition, inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not a documented position; the movement sits on the far right and does not seek to combine left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: No documented position; the doctrine ranks races rather than critiquing capitalist labour.

islam-incompatible.rationale: White nationalist and supremacist writing presents Islam and Muslims as alien to Western civilisation, as the Wikipedia articles on white nationalism describe.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Adherents split between Christian justifications, as in the Cornerstone Speech's appeal to Providence, and secular or pagan racialism.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents split: they favour excluding Islamic dress but not Christian symbols; no common stance.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not related to the ideology and no documented position.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic policy is secondary and varies from Nazi corporatism to free-market racialism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Supremacism holds that a dominant group must hold power by force, and the history of its regimes is one of armies and militias.

rich-first.rationale: Economics is secondary and adherents differ.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not part of the ideology and adherents split between isolationist and alliance-based views.

dynastic-succession.rationale: White supremacist movements have included monarchist and republican strands (e.g. Nazi Fuhrerprinzip, Confederate republic); the sources give no common position.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: adherents typically favour private property and distrust cooperative or state redistribution, but credit is not addressed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from nationalist hostility to outside control of the state; the sources do not discuss lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: Historically the movement has rejected both universal suffrage and wealth tests in favour of race; Southern states used property and tax qualifications as tools, so no single answer is inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: the ideology ranks groups by innate capacity and rejects equality of the sexes in ordinary form; the sources give no explicit treatment of ecofeminism.

reification.rationale: Inferred: a Marxist concept that adherents would reject as left-wing analysis; the sources do not discuss it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: adherents have complained about elite and minority-owned media, yet also defend property rights, so the idea is contested and not stated in the sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Nazi racial law and Jim Crow gave officials wide discretion and separate legal treatment by race, which contradicts equal standing laws; adherents more broadly claim law and order.

racial-franchise.rationale: The profile centres on restricting political rights to the dominant race; the Cornerstone Speech and Jim Crow disfranchisement state it directly.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents use online platforms for propaganda but prefer racially restricted deliberation, so a mild no is inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's secrecy and hostility to transparency of its own organisations and distrust of institutions.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religious supremacisms and racial purity doctrines favour restricting intermarriage; the sources document race-mixing bans, so a mild yes is inferred for religion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from supremacist hostility to the targeted minority; documented boycotts such as the Nazi 1933 boycott of Jewish shops show the practice, though the sources cover them thinly.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical view that authority belongs to the superior group; ordinary-citizen sortition fits poorly with that.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Where supremacists invoke religion they typically treat inherited doctrine as fixed authority for the group's claims; inferred and varied.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: No documented economic doctrine; white supremacists have varied between populist anti-finance and pro-property positions, so this is inferred as neutral.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Modern white nationalism generally treats homosexuality as degenerate and a threat to racial reproduction; inferred, as the sources do not address military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Supremacism is not atheist by doctrine and often claims religious or civilizational sanction, so state atheism is inferred as disfavoured.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Jim Crow and Confederate order relied on policing and imprisonment to enforce hierarchy; abolition is inferred as flatly contrary to that.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The Cornerstone Speech and Jim Crow rested on the dominant group holding all authority, so sharing executive power with other communities contradicts the core claim.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Adherents tend to prefer private and in-group aid over state programmes that reach targeted groups; inferred from that resentment.

term-limits.rationale: No supremacist position on term limits is documented; this is inferred as neutral.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegable, revocable voting is a radical-democratic device with no place in supremacist thought, which restricts the franchise by group; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Stoddard and Grant feared racial decline rather than extinction, and the movement has no stated line on existential-risk policy; inferred as neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Supremacist movements are typically patriarchal and traditionalist, so equal religious office for women is inferred as disfavoured.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Patriarchal family order is typical of the movement, though not stated in the opened sources; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: White supremacism seeks restricted immigration and a racially defined polity, so political voice for foreigners is rejected.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: economic questions are largely unaddressed, and defence of private property and a hierarchical order points against state price controls.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine does not address intellectual property, and its defence of established hierarchy points against abolition.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Nazi organised youth movements and racial training, documented in the profile's Nazi sources.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the doctrine is about racial hierarchy and not about weapons basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; supremacists who stress national sovereignty and those who favour white-world alliances differ.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: adherents deny or minimise genocides committed by white-supremacist regimes, though this is not stated in the sources opened.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Economic questions are largely unaddressed by the doctrine and adherents differ across the property-versus-work divide.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Cornerstone Speech, slavery, Jim Crow and Nazi racial law show the doctrine accepts violence to maintain racial rule.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: white nationalism claims an ancestral, continuous racial nation, though the sources do not state it as such.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: the ranking of groups by innate capacity rests on biological essentialism, so social construction of sex would be rejected.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: a fixed biological hierarchy of groups goes with fixed categories, and feminism is not part of the doctrine.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: white nationalist movements commemorate their dead as martyrs, though the sources do not discuss this.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: Stoddard's racial-struggle framing and religious supremacisms cast the contest between groups as a moral or world-historical struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: white nationalism seeks an ethnostate gathering its people, not a homeland that serves a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine seeks racial rule and a racially defined state directly, as the Jim Crow and Nazi sources show.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: the Christian-identity and traditionalist strands use male-centred religious language, but the sources do not address it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine is hierarchical and not feminist, so judging scripture by women's full humanity would not be adopted.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The doctrine seeks authority for the dominant race and exclusion of others from political and economic power, as Jim Crow and Nazi racial law show.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: white nationalism aims at racially defined states and separation of peoples, though the sources do not discuss merging administrative regions.

independent-unions.rationale: The sources do not address labour organisation; neutral is inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Socialism is not a framework this ideology uses, and its sources stress other authorities than working-class rule, so mild disagreement is inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral is inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral is inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Community ownership of production is outside the ideology's stated programme, so mild disagreement is inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Delegate-only confederations of local assemblies conflict with the ideology's emphasis on national or group unity; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Traditional family roles in the ideology's sources suggest mild agreement; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral is inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral is inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral is inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral is inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Individuals are ranked and valued by group membership and may be subordinated, excluded or killed for the group's ends, which contradicts the claim that no person is a mere means.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed directly; neutral is inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed directly; neutral is inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral is inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral is inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: White supremacism holds that races have distinct and unequal interests and that the dominant race must organise to secure its position, as in Grant's and Stoddard's work and white nationalism.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in race is central, usually extended to claimed superiority, as the white supremacy and white nationalism accounts document.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Colonialism, conquest and Nazi expansion were justified on racial hierarchy, so adherents do not limit force to defence; inferred from that record.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Supremacists define the group by race or descent, so a shared language alone does not make a nation for them.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from segregationist and white-nationalist aims of separate political and social arrangements by group; not about religious electorates specifically.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: White-nationalist writing, including Stoddard and Grant, casts outside forces and rival races as threats to the nation's survival.

free-public-college.rationale: No documented programme; adherents typically oppose spending that benefits the groups they target.

pollution-taxes.rationale: No documented programme; inferred from opposition to new taxes and to internationally agreed controls.

future-generations.rationale: Grant and Stoddard did stress preserving the racial stock for the future, but the sources show no wider duty to the Earth, and adherents differ.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Supremacism ranks groups by rank and sex roles, and would not give women's typical values extra weight; inferred, not documented in the sources.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from its militarism and glorification of national and racial strength; not documented in the sources here.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from its authoritarian and conspiratorial tendencies, which favour confidential statecraft; not documented.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from nationalist economic protectionism in white-nationalist movements; no direct source.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: White supremacist movements prize private arms and militias for defending the in-group, so they resist a strict state monopoly outside regimes they control; inferred from vigilante traditions.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Supremacism stresses hierarchy and obedience and glorifies conflict for the dominant group; refusal of orders is not part of it, inferred from its principles.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Economics is secondary; the movement's right-wing mainstream is hostile to unions, though some strands favour 'racially united' labour. Inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: No documented programme; adherents resent state transfers that they believe reach disfavoured groups, inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not addressed and adherents are split between laissez-faire and welfare-for-the-in-group views.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Stoddard and Grant frame the world order as a white-dominated hierarchy to be defended against rising non-white peoples, so reshaping it in favour of developing countries runs against the core doctrine.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Supremacists mostly want to capture the state for the dominant group, as with Jim Crow or Nazi law, not destroy it, though revolutionary strands exist.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Supremacism prescribes a fixed hierarchical order and racially defined political community rather than open pluralism; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; some strands link race to land and nature, others are indifferent.

sacred-nation.rationale: White nationalism treats the racially defined nation as an enduring community whose preservation gives meaning, but supremacism as a whole centres race or group more than the nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: No documented position; adherents typically oppose benefits they see as going to groups they rank lower, inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The doctrine accepts domination of subordinate groups as natural and so rejects the idea that it is exploitation; the regional framing itself is not discussed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Supremacism holds that groups differ in innate capacity and rank, as in Stoddard and Grant and the Cornerstone Speech's claim that equality is false, which contradicts a common nature grounding equal dignity and rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Movements distrust mainstream and state media as hostile and prefer their own outlets; inferred, not documented as a formal position.

religions-one-truth.rationale: White supremacism is often tied to Christian exclusivism or to racial religion, both of which reject a common truth in all faiths; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Interwar and Nazi-era agrarian blood-and-soil policies guaranteed farm prices, but the sources do not cover this directly; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Supremacists favour strength against rival powers, so disarmament is rejected; inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement ranks race above class and has attacked independent labour parties; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Supremacists often cite the practice as proof of other cultures' barbarism and would back a ban; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Historically patriarchal, yet modern white nationalists are split on women's rights; inferred as split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language naming is not addressed; the ideology is indifferent.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology is indifferent to regulation methods.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Supremacism favours its own hierarchy and racial state, not customary chiefs of other groups; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Eco-fascist strands favour it while others are indifferent, so adherents are split; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Hard-line punishment suits an authoritarian order; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Supremacists mostly want restricted immigration rather than assimilation, so adherents are split on this requirement; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not a documented topic; Jim Crow-era white supremacists and modern white nationalists mostly favoured open-shop, anti-union labour arrangements, so a mild lean to voluntary membership is inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: Jim Crow regimes used voting restrictions to exclude Black citizens, and modern white nationalists back strict proof of citizenship to limit non-white participation.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: white supremacists favoured the dominance of their own group's tradition, usually Protestant Christianity, over equal standing for others; religion is secondary to race.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Stoddard calls democracy a danger when it admits unequal races to equal power, so supremacists hold that free elections do not suffice and rule must stay with the dominant group.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: traditionalist supremacism upheld marriage and sexual norms to protect racial 'purity', though it is not a core stated position.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: authoritarian and Jim Crow-era supremacist regimes accepted suppressing communication to maintain order; no direct statement exists, as the internet postdates the classic texts.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: no documented welfare programme; supremacists resent transfers reaching targeted groups and favour keeping selective, group-restricted benefits over a universal payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Adherents are split: Stoddard and Jim Crow-era writers praised women as racial mothers while some white-nationalist strands back female suffrage for white women; the position is not stated.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: white supremacism claims to defend Christian civilisation and does not blame religion for women's status; no direct source addresses it.

race-social-construct.rationale: Supremacists hold that races are real biological groupings with innate differences in capacity; Stoddard's whole case rests on this, and the Cornerstone Speech asserts it as natural fact.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: the dominant strand favours traditional gender roles and would see state equality bodies as unnecessary; the sources do not discuss it.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not a defining issue; the settler-colonial record of white supremacism treated land taken from native peoples as rightfully the settlers' own, so mild agreement is inferred.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not addressed in its core texts; its nationalist wing resists outside judgment of its own leaders' conduct, inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The strand is split: some white supremacists such as Christian Identity groups read scripture literally, while others are secular or neopagan.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed directly; the ideology prioritises group hierarchy over equality, and traditional gender roles are common, inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Not addressed directly; white supremacism has been anti-communist, though some Nazi economic controls differed, so the answer is inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Not addressed; Confederate and Nazi systems used various offices, so no consistent position is inferred.

national-church-status.rationale: Not a defining issue; white supremacist movements often tie identity to a national or Christian heritage, so mild support is inferred.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Racially defined states and segregation are favoured, so autonomy for minority regions is inferred to be opposed, though segregated homelands were sometimes offered.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; plebiscites were used selectively by Nazi Germany and rejected where they would empower targeted groups, so no answer is inferred.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic; colonial rule itself was justified by white supremacy, but borders after independence are not a documented theme.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; adherents hold no common view on frugality or self-sufficiency.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed directly, but the ideology's ranking of groups and history of dispossessing native peoples point strongly against protecting indigenous territorial claims, inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed directly; the ideology has stressed traditional gender roles and rejects equal obligation, so this is inferred.

missingStatements.text: People of races regarded as inferior should be denied equal political rights, such as voting and citizenship.
missingStatements.rationale: Confederate doctrine held Black subordination natural, and the 1790 Naturalization Act and Jim Crow excluded non-whites from full citizenship; no existing statement asks about unequal political rights directly.

notes: Other supremacisms would answer differently, notably religious supremacism on scripture and religion in public life, and Han or Hutu strands on territory. Economic answers vary widely across white supremacist strands and are low confidence.
